decisions.decision: The defect is confirmed by measurement, not by reading. Simulating the current evidenceKey() over the real tree at fa38f0f and appending one byte to internal/application/service.go leaves the keys of runner (8d93b996c6...), reconciler (b2b1600b4f...), api (5db5722da2...), control-plane (e30e004126...) and store-firestore (7846a92cf9...) bit-for-bit identical. Under the algorithm specified in d2 the same one-byte edit moves all five. Record those two measurements in the evidence: the flaw statement and the fix statement are the same experiment run twice.
decisions.rationale: docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md line 232 and ts-v2-045's blocked transition assert the defect; neither measured it. A remediation whose only witness is the assertion it was built from is the class of work G3 rejects. The probe is also the cheapest possible regression test for the property that actually matters, so it becomes a permanent test (A9) rather than a one-off observation.

decisions.decision:
Replace evidenceKey() with this exact algorithm. (1) closure(m,id): seed a visited set with id, then repeatedly pop and expand by BOTH m[x].dependencies and m[x].verification_dependencies until the set is closed; return the ids sorted with sort.Strings. (2) patterns(m,id): for each id in that sorted closure, append roots + public_contracts + contract_dependencies; deduplicate and sort.Strings. (3) UNCONDITIONAL is the literal, sorted path list ["Makefile", "ci/components.json", "ci/key-closure.json", "devbox.json", "devbox.lock", "go.mod", "go.sum"]. (4) files = sort.Strings(git -C root ls-files split on newline, blanks dropped). (5) h = sha256; write "agentic-loop/evidence-key/v2 "; write "component:: "; write "closure:: " where j = strings.Join(closureIDs, ","); then for each p in files that is in UNCONDITIONAL or matched by some pattern, read root/p (on os.IsNotExist continue, unchanged from today), write "file::

::", then b, then " "; finally write "check:::: ". (6) key = hex(h.Sum(nil)).
decisions.rationale: Every dependency-derived input is now the depended-on component's own file set rather than its public_contracts, which is what makes the key move at all: 17 of the 23 components declare public_contracts as the empty list, so the existing loop over dep.PublicContracts contributes zero bytes for every dependency in the repository except api, control-plane, ci and contracts. Length framing before every variable-length field removes a real ambiguity in the current code, which writes path bytes immediately followed by content bytes with no separator, so (path "ab", content "c") and (path "a", content "bc") hash identically. Hashing the resolved closure id list makes a dependency-list edit move the key even when it adds no new file, which is required for the manifest itself to be part of the attested surface. Determinism is structural: no map is ever iterated, every list passes through sort.Strings, and the only external call is git ls-files, whose output is index order (already path-sorted) and is re-sorted anyway.

decisions.decision: The closure is fully transitive over the union of dependencies and verification_dependencies, with no distinction between the two once the walk starts. The refinement that traverses verification_dependencies only at the root and continues by dependencies alone is deliberately rejected.
decisions.rationale: The coarse rule is a strict superset of every refinement, so its sufficiency needs no case analysis: any file that can change the outcome of a component's check is inside the closure because it is inside the closure of something the check compiles. The refinement is sound for Go compilation (an external test package of d is never linked into c) but stops being sound the moment a check target runs a dependency's test packages, which several targets already do: component-runner runs ./internal/domain, component-reconciler runs ./internal/application ./internal/domain, component-release runs ./internal/domain. Proving the refinement therefore requires a per-target argument that must be re-proved whenever the Makefile changes, while the coarse rule needs no argument at all. Measured cost of the coarse rule at fa38f0f: closure size 1 for 12 of 23 components, 2-5 for another 6, and 11-15 for the five deepest (api, control-plane, reconciler, runner, store-firestore); the file counts are 172-188 out of 1000+ tracked files, so the key stays far from all_on_change. product_orchestrator already accepted the extra re-verification as the price.

decisions.decision: Extend the unconditional set from [ci/components.json, go.mod, go.sum, devbox.lock] to also include Makefile, devbox.json and ci/key-closure.json.
decisions.rationale: Every component's verification entrypoint is a make target whose recipe lives in the Makefile, so editing component-runner's package list today changes what the runner evidence attests while leaving the runner key fixed: the same class of defect as the one this task exists to fix, one level up. Makefile is in all_on_change, which selects the component but does not invalidate its recorded evidence, and those are different guarantees. devbox.json declares the packages and the scripts that devbox run --pure executes; devbox.lock pins the resolved versions but does not record a script edit, so a devbox.json-only change is invisible to the key today. validation.md section 11 already requires 'test source／runner、lockfile／toolchain／Devbox 等の環境定義' in the key; the implementation omits two of the three. ci/key-closure.json is added because d10 makes it the published form of the closure.

decisions.decision: Refactor evidenceKey into an injectable pair: ListTracked(root) ([]string, error) that shells out to git ls-files, and EvidenceKeyFromFiles(root string, files []string, m Manifest, c Component) (string, error) that does everything else. EvidenceKeyWithManifest becomes the composition of the two. Delete the manifest-free EvidenceKey(root, c) entirely.
decisions.rationale: The key-sensitivity tests required by d9 need to compare two trees that differ in one byte, and building two throwaway git repositories per assertion makes those tests slow, dependent on git's presence inside devbox run --pure, and sensitive to whatever global git config the runner inherits. With the file list injected, the test writes a temp directory, passes an explicit file list, and mutates one file: no git, no subprocess, fully hermetic. EvidenceKey(root, c) has no caller outside planner.go and cannot compute a closure without a manifest, so keeping it would leave a function in the package whose result is a key that no longer means what its name says.

decisions.decision: dependencies is the non-test import graph plus contract-file reads, and stays the acyclic DAG that Affected() walks. Set it to exactly: api [application domain infra runner web]; application [domain infra]; control-plane [api application reconciler runner store-firestore]; infra []; internal-contracts [contracts]; reconciler [application domain infra]; release [contracts domain]; runner [application domain internal-contracts provider update]; store-firestore [application domain infra runner]; store-memory [application domain infra]; task-ledger [contracts]; and the empty list for ci, contracts, docs, domain, environment, legacy-import, provider, repository-meta, scheduler, tooling, update, web. Two removals matter: reconciler loses store-firestore, and infra loses store-firestore.
decisions.rationale: Measured against the real import graph at fa38f0f, and verified acyclic by a depth-first walk before being written down. reconciler -> store-firestore is not an import, not a contract read and not a check-target relation, so it is padding; leaving it in would make the coverage assertion of d9 pass on an edge nothing justifies. infra -> store-firestore is the real edge reversed: internal/quota (owned by infra) imports nothing from the module, while internal/store/firestore/store.go and runner.go import internal/quota. Keeping the reversed edge alongside the true one closes the ring infra -> store-firestore -> runner -> application -> infra, and Validate rejects cycles, so the reversed edge must go. Nothing is lost: infra/** is in all_on_change, so any infra change already selects every component, and firestore.indexes.json is a store-firestore root.

decisions.decision: Add one new manifest field, verification_dependencies, defined as the components whose sources participate in this component's verification without being one of its non-test imports. It has exactly three mechanical sources: (a) test-only cross-component imports, (b) module import paths that a test hands to an out-of-band build or run instead of importing, and (c) packages or scripts executed by the component's check target that another component owns. It is NOT consulted by Affected(), it IS part of the d2 key closure, and it is deliberately exempt from the acyclicity check. Set it to: api [control-plane store-firestore store-memory]; application [store-memory]; contracts [internal-contracts]; infra [environment]; reconciler [provider runner store-memory]; runner [reconciler store-memory]; store-firestore [environment]; task-ledger [internal-contracts]; empty elsewhere.
decisions.rationale: The test-import graph genuinely contains cycles, so these edges cannot go into dependencies without breaking a rule validation.md section 11 states outright ('循環依存 … manifest 検証の失敗'): internal/runner/control_agent_test.go imports internal/reconciler while internal/reconciler/stop_journey_test.go imports internal/runner, and component-contracts runs ./internal/contracts, which is owned by internal-contracts, which depends on contracts. Keeping them out of Affected() is what keeps the non-goal 'do not change the affected-closure selection logic' intact, while feeding them into the key is what makes the guarantee real: reconciler's check target compiles internal/runner's test helpers, so a runner edit changes what the reconciler evidence attests and the reconciler key must move. Source (c) is why infra and store-firestore name environment: component-infra runs scripts/infra-policy.sh and scripts/infra-validate.sh and component-store-firestore runs scripts/firestore-emulator.sh, all owned by environment. Every one of these nine edges is derivable by the d8 procedure, so none of them is hand-maintained.

decisions.decision: Derive the import graph with go/parser over every tracked *.go file (parser.ImportsOnly is sufficient), reading f.Imports only. Do not use go list, and do not use a regular expression. Classify a file as test iff its name ends in _test.go. Map a component-relative directory to its owner with the manifest's own match() so ownership can never disagree with make ownership. For source (b), walk *ast.BasicLit string literals whose value is the module path or begins with the module path plus '/'. For source (c), parse the Makefile recipe lines of each component's check target for ./-prefixed package paths and for scripts/*.sh paths, and resolve each to its owning component. Require one cross-check of the derived graph against devbox run --pure -- go list -json ./... and record the comparison in the evidence.
decisions.rationale: Measured, and the measurement decided it. A regular-expression scan over the same files reports two edges that do not exist: internal/release/source_guard_test.go contains the literals .../internal/ci and .../internal/update as assertion data for the dp-v2-021 d12 import guard, so a text scan turns the guard against itself. go list is correct for imports but blind to two things this task must see: it cannot report the build-tag-excluded files that AST parsing reads anyway, and it does not see internal/api/live_local_test.go line 191, exec.Command("go", "build", "-o", binPath, ".../cmd/control-plane"), which is a real compile-time dependency of the api component's live test expressed as a string. AST parsing also avoids nesting a go-tool invocation inside go test, where GOFLAGS, GOCACHE and the environment stripping of devbox run --pure all become variables the test result depends on. The go list cross-check stays because the directory-to-import-path mapping is the one place an AST-only implementation can be silently wrong, and it costs one command.

decisions.decision: Add internal/ci/manifest_dependencies.go with three pure, exported checks, and assert all three against the real manifest plus a positive control each. (1) VerifyDependencyCoverage: for every component, declared dependencies must be a superset of the derived non-test import edges, and declared verification_dependencies union declared dependencies must be a superset of the derived source-(a)/(b)/(c) edges. (2) VerifyNoUnjustifiedEdges: any declared edge that is not derived must appear in a JustifiedEdges table with a written reason; seed it with exactly three entries (internal-contracts -> contracts, task-ledger -> contracts, release -> contracts, all contract-file reads already expressed in contract_dependencies) and a LiteralFalsePositives table with exactly two entries (internal/release/source_guard_test.go -> internal/ci and -> internal/update, assertion data for the dp-v2-021 d12 guard, never a dependency). (3) VerifyCheckTargetInsideClosure: every package and script the check target runs must be owned by a component inside the key closure. Positive controls, each its own subtest: PC1 delete one dependency from an in-memory copy of the real manifest and require (1) to fail, naming the edge; PC2 delete one JustifiedEdges entry and require (2) to fail; PC3 the AST extractor against a t.TempDir() fixture module containing a non-test import, a _test.go-only import, a build-tag-excluded file whose import must still be found, and a string literal shaped like an import path that must NOT be counted; PC4 two components differing only in how the same bytes split between path and content must get different keys; PC5 appending one byte to a dependency's file must move the consumer's key while leaving an unrelated component's key fixed; PC6 appending one byte to Makefile must move all 23 keys.
decisions.rationale: validation.md section 11 'CI 自身の検証' asks for exactly this and section 6 requires a positive control for every negative assertion. Splitting the three checks into pure functions over an injected Manifest is what makes PC1 and PC2 possible without touching a tracked file: a positive control that needs a real edit to ci/components.json cannot run inside make check and would be recorded as an assertion instead of a measurement. Check (2) is not decoration; without it the whole coverage assertion is trivially satisfiable by declaring that every component depends on every other, which would make the key maximally coarse and the manifest worthless as a description of the system. PC5's second half is the non-vacuity control: without it a bug that made every key depend on every file would pass the first half.

decisions.decision: cmd/ci-plan gains --closure-out <path>; make key-closure writes ci/key-closure.json containing version, key_version, the sorted unconditional list, and one entry per component with its sorted closure ids and its sorted pattern list, and nothing else. A golden test in internal/ci recomputes the file from ci/components.json and fails if the tracked bytes differ. internal/release/bundle_test.go stops reimplementing the closure and reads ci/key-closure.json instead. ci/key-closure.json must never contain an evidence key.
decisions.rationale: internal/release/bundle_test.go currently carries its own copy of the closure rule (releaseEvidenceKeyClosure, lines 274-305), which would silently keep the old semantics after this change and turn TestReleaseEvidenceKeyClosureAndUnguardedAllowlist into a test of a rule nobody uses. The obvious fix, importing internal/ci, is forbidden: dp-v2-021 d12 forbids internal/release from importing internal/ci or internal/update in test files or otherwise, and internal/release/source_guard_test.go enforces it. Publishing the closure as data under ci/**, which the manifest already declares as the ci component's public contract, gives one source of truth with no import edge. Excluding keys from the file is not stylistic: a file that contained keys and was itself hashed into every key would be an unsatisfiable fixed point, the same one validation.md section 11 documents for aggregate attestations.

decisions.decision: Adding devbox.json to the unconditional set brings it inside the release component's key closure, which requires two edits in internal/release that are consequences, not scope creep: delete the devbox.json entry from UnguardedMembers, and delete the clause in TestReleaseEvidenceKeyClosureAndUnguardedAllowlist that fails when an unguarded-role member IS covered. The surviving assertions are: every bundle member is covered or allowlisted; every guarded-role member is covered; every allowlisted glob is still uncovered.
decisions.rationale: The deleted clause encoded a fact about the old closure ('the closure is known not to reach configuration-role members'), not a property worth preserving: coverage widening is the improvement this task ships, so an assertion that fires when coverage widens is an obstacle rather than a guard. The surviving 'covered implies not allowlisted' assertion is the one that matters, because it forces the allowlist to shrink as coverage grows and it is what makes the E1 escalation in docs/operations/release-local.md self-retiring. Verified by inspection of the role table (internal/release/bundle.go lines 56-61): the release closure after this change reaches contracts/**, internal/domain/**, internal/contracts/**, internal/release/** and the seven unconditional paths, so all four guarded roles stay covered (contract, schema and api-contract via contracts/**, implementation-manifest via the unconditional list), firestore.indexes.json and firebase.json stay uncovered and allowlisted, and devbox.json is the only member that crosses over.

decisions.decision: Re-issue evidence as 24 records in one commit: 23 per-component records .agents/v2/evidence/V2-045-<component>.json with id ev-v2-045-<component>, component <component>, and evidence_key equal to that component's key at the judgment commit; plus one .agents/v2/evidence/V2-045-candidate-aggregate.json with id ev-v2-045-candidate-aggregate, component candidate-aggregate, and evidence_key equal to the sha256 of the id-sorted "<id>\n<key>\n" concatenation of all 23 keys, which is byte-for-byte the method ev-v2-040-candidate-aggregate declared. Existing records are never edited; every record here is an addition.
decisions.rationale: One aggregate is not sufficient and the reason is textual: docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md G6 requires, per component, an index entry whose own evidence_key field equals that component's key at the judgment commit. An aggregate entry's evidence_key is the composite, and the per-component keys live inside checks[].summary where G6 does not look, so an aggregate alone would leave every one of the 23 components stale for any gate that lists it as 根拠. The aggregate is still issued because G6's synthetic-component clause reads the declared composite method, because M0 and M1 cited aggregate ids directly, and because it is the only record that can carry the make candidate verdict and one base_commit for the whole surface. Append-only follows the ev-v2-057-reconciler-refresh and ev-v2-060-*-refresh precedent: rewriting ev-v2-016-runner's key would erase the first observation of a tree that really was measured, and the same index already holds four docs records and two runner records without difficulty.

decisions.decision: Follow the validation.md section 11 two-commit protocol. Commit A carries only ci/components.json, ci/key-closure.json, internal/ci/**, cmd/ci-plan/**, Makefile, internal/release/bundle.go, internal/release/bundle_test.go and the docs edits; nothing under .agents/**. All 23 keys, make check, make candidate and make evidence-all are measured at commit A and its sha is recorded as base_commit. Commit B carries only the 24 evidence records and the index entries. Run devbox run --pure -- go clean -testcache before make evidence-all. After commit B, run make check again and record the result. The residual, that commit B moves the task-ledger key away from the value the records carry, is named in the aggregate as the documented fixed point, not silently omitted and not papered over with a further record.
decisions.rationale: The protocol exists because an attestation cannot record the key of a tree that contains the attestation. Naming the residual is the only honest option: adding a third commit to record task-ledger's key at commit B just relocates the same fixed point to commit C, and V2-040 hit and documented exactly this. go clean -testcache removes the weakness ev-v2-057-reconciler-refresh had to write down in prose, that make component-<id> does not pass -count=1 and can therefore report a cached result; clearing the cache once makes every check inside make evidence-all a real execution. Re-running make check after commit B is required because gitleaks git scans committed history, so the 64-hex keys in the 24 new records are not scanned until they are committed.

decisions.decision: V2-045 does NOT issue any provider-live-claude record. It measures and reports instead. ev-v2-017-provider-live-claude declares (check b22) that its evidence_key IS the runner component's key, 8d93b996c667...; the runner key moves under d2, so that record becomes stale by its own declared method the moment commit A lands. Luna must record, as a check in the aggregate, both the old and the newly recomputed value and the fact that they differ, plus the measured intersection of commit A's diff with the file set the live exercise executes. V2-018 decides between paying a live re-run and accepting an explicitly reasoned carry-forward.
decisions.rationale: Writing a passed provider-live-claude record without running the real claude CLI is exactly the substitution G3 rejects and the acceptance rule 'do not write a verification you did not execute' forbids; changing the declared composite method after the fact so the old value still matches is the cosmetic remediation this task was created to avoid. Neither is a Tech Lead's call and neither is Luna's: G3 places live-versus-local on product_orchestrator and the gate. What V2-045 can do is make the decision cheap, by handing V2-018 the recomputed value and the evidence that commit A touches only ci/**, internal/ci/**, cmd/ci-plan/**, Makefile, internal/release/bundle*.go, docs/** and ci/key-closure.json, none of which is on the claude invocation path.

decisions.decision: Explicitly out of scope, with the reason: splitting internal/quota out of the infra component (a boundary redesign, forbidden by the task's non_goals, and unnecessary once the reversed edge is removed); any change to Affected(), to all_on_change, or to the ownership rule; adding api -> control-plane to dependencies rather than verification_dependencies; adding scripts/** to the unconditional set; adding ci/key-closure.json to the release bundle's implementation-manifest role; and editing docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md, which two other Tech Leads are writing to concurrently.
decisions.rationale: Each of these is a defensible change that is not this task's outcome. internal/quota inside infra is odd (a Go package sharing a component with Terraform) but the reversed-edge removal in d6 makes the DAG correct without touching the boundary, so the split has no remaining justification here. scripts/** stays out of the unconditional set because the specific scripts each check target runs are already reached through the environment component by d7 source (c), which is narrower and derivable. Adding ci/key-closure.json to the release bundle changes the bundle digest surface and therefore the release contract, which needs its own task.

verification: devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -v ./internal/ci ./cmd/ci-plan (timeout 900s): the three manifest checks pass on the real manifest and every one of PC1 through PC6 fails-when-it-should, each as a named subtest.

devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/release (timeout 900s): TestReleaseEvidenceKeyClosureAndUnguardedAllowlist passes against ci/key-closure.json with the devbox.json allowlist entry deleted, and TestSourceGuardMatcherIsVerified still passes, proving internal/release gained no import of internal/ci.
devbox run --pure -- go list -json ./... (timeout 600s), compared against the AST-derived graph: the one-off cross-check required by d8. Divergences must be explained in the evidence, not silenced.
devbox run --pure -- make key-closure (timeout 300s) followed by git diff --exit-code ci/key-closure.json: the tracked golden file is what the generator produces.
devbox run --pure -- make ownership (timeout 300s): ci/key-closure.json and every new Go file have exactly one owning component.
devbox run --pure -- make check (timeout 2400s) at commit A, and again after commit B so gitleaks git scans the committed evidence.

devbox run --pure -- go clean -testcache then devbox run --pure -- make evidence-all EVIDENCE_TASK_ID=V2-045 EVIDENCE_CORRELATION_ID=v2-045-dependency-surface (timeout 3600s) at commit A, then devbox run --pure -- make candidate (timeout 900s) returning {"candidate":true}.
devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys (timeout 600s) at commit A: the 23 keys the records must carry, read only after git add so no new file is invisible to git ls-files.

devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts (timeout 600s): TestTaskPacketsValidate accepts both V2-045 packets and TestActiveEvidenceIndex accepts all 24 new records and their index entries.
risks: ev-v2-017-provider-live-claude goes stale by its own declared method at commit A (d14). This is the single highest-consequence effect of the task and it is not resolvable inside it: the resolution costs either real claude quota or an explicit product_orchestrator ruling. If V2-018 will not accept a carry-forward, V2-045 must land anyway and the live re-run becomes a separate task, because reverting V2-045 does not make the key correct.

Two other Tech Leads are writing V2-022, V2-030, V2-058 and V2-059 packets, and .agents/v2/evidence/index.json is the file every implementer touches. Twenty-four new entries make the conflict surface unusually large. The entries must be re-added after any rebase and every evidence_hash recomputed on the final bytes; resolving the conflict in favour of either side wholesale would drop another task's entry and fail TestActiveEvidenceIndex.

The api and control-plane closures reach 15 of 23 components and 188 files. If that turns out to make the selective-CI feedback loop unacceptably wide in practice, the correct response is the d3 refinement with a per-check-target soundness argument, not narrowing the manifest, and it needs its own task with its own measurement.

The three deletions this task makes (reconciler -> store-firestore, infra -> store-firestore, the devbox.json UnguardedMembers entry) all narrow something. validation.md section 11 says '影響範囲を狭める変更ほど強い根拠を要求する', so each one needs its measurement in the evidence: no import, no contract read, no check-target relation for the first two, and now-covered for the third.

PC5 and PC6 depend on the d5 refactor landing cleanly. If EvidenceKeyFromFiles cannot be threaded without touching cmd/ci-plan's flag handling more than expected, the temptation is to test key sensitivity by mutating the real tree. That must be refused: a test that edits a tracked file cannot run inside make check and would leave the property unverified in CI.

make check runs component-store-firestore, which needs the Firestore emulator. If it is unavailable the whole entrypoint is red for a reason unrelated to this change; that is an environment stop, not a failure to record as partial.
